one_liner: Task-based supernodal sparse Cholesky (Fortran) on OpenMP, StarPU or PaRSEC; papers report parity with HSL_MA87, not a speedup.
what_it_does: Solves sparse symmetric positive definite systems in three phases: analyse (delegated to SPRAL SSIDS, which builds the assembly tree with METIS ordering and nemin amalgamation), factor (LL^T) and solve. The Fortran API (spllt_analyse, spllt_factor, spllt_wait, spllt_solve with akeep/fkeep handles and a spllt_options type) follows the same analyse/factor/solve shape as HSL_MA87 but uses its own types, so it is not a call-for-call replacement. A C binding in interfaces/C/spllt_data_ciface.F90 exports spllt_analyse, spllt_factor, spllt_prepare_solve, spllt_solve and spllt_chkerr over spllt_options_t/spllt_inform_t structs and lower-triangle, 1-based CSC input.
how_it_is_fast: Each supernode is cut into nb x nb tiles and the factorization becomes a DAG of tile tasks (factorize diagonal block, triangular solve, intra-node update, inter-node update_between), the same DAG-based scheme as HSL_MA87. A runtime system schedules the tasks as their dependencies resolve: OpenMP 4 tasks with depend clauses, StarPU in sequential-task-flow style, or PaRSEC with a parameterized task graph. Tree pruning (prune_tree, on by default) folds small subtrees into single coarse tasks to limit scheduling overhead, and the solve phase also runs as a DAG of forward and backward substitution tasks. The goal is to match MA87 performance while staying portable across runtimes, not to beat it.
when_to_use: Research on runtime systems for sparse direct solvers: the same Cholesky algorithm implemented on OpenMP, StarPU and PaRSEC, which you can compare side by side.
Multicore SPD factorization where HSL_MA87's licence is a problem and a BSD-3-Clause code with roughly MA87-level speed (per the authors' papers, snippet only) is acceptable.

Fortran codes that already depend on SPRAL and want a Cholesky-only path whose tasks can be handed to StarPU or PaRSEC; CMake also has USE_GPU (MAGMA, CUDA) and USE_MPI options, status not documented.
when_not_to_use: Indefinite or unsymmetric matrices: Cholesky only, no pivoting.
When you need evidence of a speedup: the repo has no numbers, the papers claim parity with HSL_MA87, and no comparison with CHOLMOD, PARDISO or PaStiX was found.

Current toolchains without patching: gfortran 10+ stops on a rank mismatch in spllt_kernels_mod.F90 unless -fallow-argument-mismatch is added (issue #4); CI only ever ran gcc-6 on Travis, and the code has been unmaintained since 2019.

C or C++ projects wanting a small dependency: you need a Fortran compiler, SPRAL, METIS 5.1, hwloc, BLAS/LAPACK and a runtime, and the CMake build has no install target (install(TARGETS spllt) is commented out).

integration.dependencies: SPRAL (SSIDS analyse), METIS 5.1, BLAS/LAPACK (MKL in the README examples), hwloc, and one of StarPU, PaRSEC or an OpenMP 4.0 compiler; optional CUDA and MAGMA for USE_GPU
integration.min_toolchain: Fortran 2003 compiler with iso_c_binding plus C compiler, CMake 2.6+; gfortran 6 in CI, gfortran 10+ needs -fallow-argument-mismatch; GNU or Intel compilers for the OpenMP build
integration.platforms: Linux multicore x86-64 (KNL build option); other platforms not documented
integration.thread_safety: not documented; parallelism is internal to spllt_factor and spllt_solve through the chosen runtime
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — same analyse/factor/solve structure as HSL_MA87, but different derived types and option names, so call sites must be rewritten

gotchas: The default CMake build type is RelWithDebInfo, which appends -fcheck=all -Wall to the Fortran flags, so an unconfigured build runs with array-bounds and runtime checks on; use -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release before timing. The default RUNTIME is STF (sequential), options ncpu defaults to 1 and nb to 16, so parallel speed needs -DRUNTIME=OMP|StarPU|Parsec plus explicit ncpu and a larger tile size.

The OpenMP build adds -fopenmp or -qopenmp only when the C++ compiler is GNU or Intel; with any other compiler (Clang) CMake just sets an ERROR variable and continues, producing a build without OpenMP.

The OpenMP benchmark driver drivers/spllt_omp_bench.F90 does not compile against the current API (wrong spllt_solve and spllt_compute_solve_dep signatures, issue #1), and after the reporter's fix the run hit an out-of-bounds access on fkeep%sbc; issues #1-#4 from 2022 have no maintainer reply.

The C binding's spllt_inform_t returns num_flops and num_factor as 32-bit C int while the Fortran fields are 64-bit, so they overflow on any sizeable factorization; it also expects 1-based CSC (nnz is read as ptr(n+1)-1 and the array_base option is commented out).
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick SpLLT only to study or reuse one Cholesky algorithm across OpenMP, StarPU and PaRSEC. For production SPD factorization, BaSpaCho (measured gains over CHOLMOD) or SPRAL SSIDS (maintained, also handles indefinite systems) are better-supported choices, and SyLVER, from the same NLAFET project, is a related DAG-based symmetric solver.
verified_claims_summary: No numbers exist in the repo or on any reachable page. The authors' papers (Duff, Hogg and Lopez, NACO 2018, doi 10.3934/naco.2018014; a PaRSEC/PTG paper in IJHPCA, doi 10.1177/1094342019888567), seen only as search snippets because epubs.stfc.ac.uk and aimsciences.org are blocked, say the OpenMP, StarPU and PaRSEC versions perform comparably to HSL_MA87 on a multicore machine, which is parity; compiler, BLAS and hardware are unknown. The comparison drivers in the repo (drivers/run_ma87.f90 with metis_order, drivers/spllt_test.F90 via spllt_analyse, which forces ssids_opt%ordering = 1) both use METIS ordering, so open issue #2's ordering concern does not apply to them.
status_note: Abandoned since 2019-08-23 (710 commits, 6 stars, four 2022 issues unanswered, Travis CI on gcc-6 only); BSD-3-Clause and usable as a research reference, but expect to patch the build for gfortran 10+ and to supply SPRAL, METIS 5.1, hwloc and a runtime yourself.
